fact: A World Bank blog says Morocco launched in 2007 a portal for electronic tenders, bid submission and reverse auctions, and from 2020 to 2022 required all bidders to use the public procurement portal.
A World Bank blog says the share of bids submitted electronically in Morocco rose from 15% in December 2019 to 68% in June 2022.
Arrete 1692-23, in force 1 September 2023, provides that bids are filed and withdrawn electronically through the public procurement portal, with electronic opening and evaluation, per Le Matin.
An Al3omk op-ed says the precautionary suspension of the Treasury's public-procurement portal in late October 2026 forced tender procedures to be rescheduled and bid deadlines postponed.
